The [[Jungle/Legends|jungle]]-[[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nallastia]] was home to the '''fortress''' of its [[Skull Queen]], [[Quenelle]]. The Skull Queen welcomed several [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to her fortress during their [[Mission to Fondor (Separatist Crisis)|mission to Fondor]] in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]].

==Description==
The Skull Queen's fortress was a massive ten-story compound carved from the black [[Volcano/Legends|volcanic]] rock of [[Mount Octan]].

During a standard Nallastian night, the phenomenon known as ''planet light'' (reflected light from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]], as it reflected its [[Fondor system/Legends|system's]] [[Fondor (star)|sun]], rising over the jungle) bathed the [[Satellite/Legends|satellite]]-[[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] and the staggered rows of fortress battlements and ancient megaliths in a blueish glow.

Three massive megaliths, each of which were eight meters tall, stood in triangular formation in the midst of a field guarded by 50 [[Nallastian]] [[warrior]]s clad in reptilian skins and animal-bone armor, bearing primitive energy-projectile launchers (although a few held contemporary [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] weapons): the plot of land between the stones was littered with bones, both human and alien. The stone triangulation—called the [[Trinity Stones]]—was the basis for the [[Force field/Legends|energy field]] (a lunar [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] [[Vortex/Legends|vortex]]) that served as the inescapable deathbed for offenders of Nallastian law: they had to wait but 90 [[Standard minute/Legends|standard minutes]] to be crushed by the stones, which were [[Magnet/Legends|magnetically]] drawn to one another. Once the megaliths met, they repelled back to their original positions.

==Behind the scenes==
[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Bultar Swan/Legends|Bultar Swan's]] comment to 18-year-old [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] at the [[Skull Queen]]'s fortress that ''"Jedi don't have nightmares"'' serves as a precursor reference to Anakin's identical line of dialogue with [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] as he stands on the east balcony of the [[Naberrie family/Legends|Naberrie family's]] [[Varykino/Legends|Varykino]] lodge (in both ''Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones'' [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novel]] and [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|screenplay]]<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones novelization">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref>) that appears to directly quote Swan from Skywalker's [[Skull Queen's fortress#Disturbing dreams|memory]] of their [[Skull Queen's fortress#No nightmares|discussion]] about '[[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Dream/Legends|dreams]]' during their [[Mission to Fondor (Separatist Crisis)|mission to Fondor]] some months earlier.
